Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Team
Ramp builds software that moves real money — corporate cards, bill payments, reimbursements, accounting integrations, and travel. Our customers rely on us to keep their operations running, and our CX team is the frontline when something needs to be resolved fast.
Premier Support is the dedicated support team for Ramp's largest and most complex customers - the Enterprise and Strategic accounts running global, multi-entity finance operations on Ramp. Our specialists support these accounts with real depth: they know the businesses, stakeholders, and systems, and they're the people the customer comes to when something matters. It's high-touch, relationship-led support.
About the Role
Ramp is hiring an Associate Manager to lead Premier Support. This is a small team of senior specialists - six today, scaling meaningfully, who are the daily point of contact for the accounts Ramp can least afford to get wrong.
You'll own the people and the performance. That means coaching specialists who operate with real autonomy, hold a high bar for quality and responsiveness when the stakes are high, and are the person your team escalates to when an account is experiencing challenges. You'll partner daily with the Account Managers who own the strategy for these same accounts - they own the account direction, you own the support experience that makes it possible.
This team is new. The playbook exists but it isn't finished, and you'll be shaping it. That means you need to be someone who can build and lead at the same time: designing the operating rhythm, spotting where the model breaks before it breaks, and having a contingency ready when something doesn't land. You'll be trusted with a lot early, and you'll have a manager who has built these teams from scratch and stays close.
This is a people-leadership job first. We're looking for someone genuinely passionate about managing people and building strong, solid teams. Someone who finds the craft of leadership itself interesting, not just the outcomes it produces.
What You'll Do
• Lead and develop a team of senior specialists. Run weekly 1:1s, give feedback that changes behavior, and build development plans that grow real ownership and judgment. Know your people well enough to make coaching specific.

• Own performance directly. Set a clear bar, recognize and grow your strongest people, and address gaps early and honestly. You'll have the hard conversations yourself, with a plan and a follow-through.

• Own your team's results. Quality, responsiveness, and SLA delivery across the accounts your team supports - plus the day-to-day mechanics that get you there: triage by account risk, load balancing, coverage, and on-call rotation.

• Own escalations. Be the point of accountability when a strategic account escalates - driving it to resolution, keeping partners informed, and making sure it gets raised cleanly to Product or Engineering when it needs to.

• Partner with Account Management. Work shoulder-to-shoulder on shared accounts: surfacing risk, feeding product and account signals back, and making Premier a partner they rely on.

• Use data to decide. Read the quality, SLA, escalation, and volume trends; find the root cause; turn it into coaching or a process change.

• Build what's missing. Turn recurring patterns from your accounts into durable playbooks, documentation, and processes. Manage capacity as the book grows, so quality scales faster than headcount.

• Work with AI tools daily. Ramp is actively building AI into CX operations. You'll adopt and champion AI-powered workflows, help your team get fluent, and shape how these tools evolve. Comfort with new technology isn't optional - we are all builders at Ramp.

About the Role

Security at Cloudflare is a focused team committed to helping secure both Cloudflare and our customers. The Threat Detection Automation and Intelligence Team is responsible for identifying, understanding and detecting threats to Cloudflare.

We are seeking an experienced Threat Intelligence Engineer with experience with machine learning data science to join our proactive security team. This role is a critical blend of two disciplines: leveraging Threat Intelligence (TI) to understand the adversary, and then applying advanced Machine Learning and engineering principles to rapidly and effectively defend our organization. The ideal candidate will transform raw threat data into actionable security measures and automated defenses, significantly reducing our mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to respond (MTTR) to sophisticated cyber threats.

• Intelligence Collection & Analysis: Proactively research, collect, and analyze threat intelligence from various sources (OSINT, commercial feeds, dark web, and internal security events) to understand the current and emerging threat landscape.

• IOC/IOA Management: Engineer the ingestion, enrichment, correlation, and contextualization of Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) and Indicators of Attack (IOAs) into security platforms.

• Automated Defense Development: Design, develop, and implement robust automation workflows and playbooks (SOAR) to streamline security operations tasks, including incident triage, alert enrichment, vulnerability management, and threat response actions.

• Tool Integration & Optimization: Integrate diverse security tools (e.g., SIEM, EDR, Cloud Security Posture Management, vulnerability scanners, Threat Intelligence Platforms) through APIs and scripting (primarily Python) to create seamless, automated feedback loops.

• Process Improvement: Identify manual, repetitive, and time-consuming security processes and engineer scalable automation solutions to increase team efficiency and operational maturity.

• Incident Response Support: Provide threat context to support the Incident Response team during active security incidents.

• Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate with Detection Engineers, Security Engineers, and Software Developers to embed security and intelligence-driven practices into the CI/CD pipeline and corporate infrastructure.

Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.

What is The Role

SONAR is the adversary research team within Elastic Security. We discover novel adversary behavior through malware reverse engineering, threat hunting, and vulnerability research, turn every discovery into protections that ship to customers, and share our work publicly through Elastic Security Labs. We want to make environments hostile to adversaries, and to put rare knowledge and tooling within reach of every defender. We are looking for a Senior Security Research Engineer to take on our hardest analysis work and help set the technical direction of the team. Our geographically dispersed team values positivity and inclusivity in the workplace, clear communication, collaborative learning, and guided mentorship.

Our research is public, and much of it is work you may already know: this team identified the supply chain compromise of the axios npm package, uncovered a new Contagious Interview campaign hiding DPRK malware inside SVG images, and published in-depth analyses of the TCLBANKER banking trojan and the PHANTOMPULSE RAT, each one paired with protections that shipped to customers. If you have a passion for taking apart what adversaries build, and would enjoy the challenge of getting that understanding into customers' hands quickly, join our growing team!

What You Will Be Doing

• Reverse engineer malware nobody has documented yet. Take apart obfuscated and packed samples across Windows, macOS, and Linux, and recover how they communicate, configure themselves, and stay hidden.

• Operate global data systems to identify and mitigate threats. Work through data from millions of endpoints to surface the activity worth investigating, build the campaign context that tells customers who is targeting them, and push mitigation back out across the fleet.

• Turn every discovery into a shipped protection, and the tooling that scales it. Author the signatures that stop what you find, and build the automation and AI-assisted workflows that make the next investigation faster than the last.

• Build your public research reputation. Publish on Elastic Security Labs, release tools and detection artifacts to our public GitHub repositories, and present at conferences. We encourage a public persona and the relationships in the research community that come with it.

• Collaborate across Elastic Security. Your discoveries become the rules and models that neighboring teams build and ship, and you will work with those teams directly on shared threat intelligence and detection engineering projects.

• Help lead the team's technical direction. Take point on investigations that run for months, raise the bar in review, and mentor researchers earlier in their careers.

What You Bring

• 6+ years of professional experience reverse engineering malware and researching adversary tradecraft, static and dynamic, across multiple executable formats (PE, ELF, Mach-O) and architectures (x86-64, ARM), including obfuscated and packed code that defeats automated tooling.

• Python development experience for research tooling and automation, plus the ability to read C and C++. Malware arrives in Rust, Go, and NodeJS too, so you are willing to learn a new runtime when a sample demands it.

• YARA authorship and hunting at scale. You write signatures that hold up against the next variant, and you can find a weak signal in a very large telemetry dataset.

• Working knowledge of the fundamentals : Windows and Linux internals, network protocols including HTTP and TLS, and enough applied cryptography to recognize what is protecting a configuration blob.

• Technical writing ability. You can turn a long investigation into a clear, public analysis that other defenders can act on.

• You have a proven track record of using AI to accelerate development, debug complex systems, and optimize code, while still owning the final outcomes.

• Proven ability to seamlessly transition between different projects, codebases, or scrum teams based on dynamic business priorities.

• A collaborative mentality, an eagerness to learn new skills and emerging technologies, and a passion for protecting the world's data from attack!

Bonus Points

• Vulnerability research or novel technique discovery, with a track record of responsible disclosure.

• Participation in CTFs such as FLARE-ON or NetWars.

• Standing in the community: maintaining an open-source security tool, speaking at conferences (e.g., Black Hat, DEF CON, CODE BLUE, Virus Bulletin), or an established publication record.

• Attribution tradecraft, including joint investigations with external intelligence partners and platforms such as MISP or OpenCTI.

• Behavioral detection engineering beyond signatures, or applying machine learning to malware classification.

• Familiarity with the Elastic Stack (Elasticsearch, Kibana) and Elastic Security.

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Japan is one of the most sophisticated enterprise technology markets in the world, and one where partners, not vendors, typically own the customer relationship. The Head of Partnerships, Japan will build and lead the team that makes Anthropic's partner ecosystem the primary route to Japanese enterprise.

You will set the partner strategy for Japan, develop the team that executes it, and own the partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, revenue and attach rate for the country. You will personally lead our most strategic partner relationships at the executive level while coaching your team to do the same across the GSI, regional SI, and reseller landscape.

This is a player-coach role for an experienced partner leader who has built and scaled partner businesses in Japan before, ideally for a US technology company entering or growing in the market. You will work day to day with the Japan sales leadership and the in-region Applied AI team, represent Japan within Anthropic's International Partnerships organisation, and carry the voice of Japanese partners and customers into our global product and go-to-market decisions.

Key responsibilities

Lead and build the team

• Hire, develop and retain a high-performing Japan partner team spanning GSI, regional SI and reseller coverage, sized and structured to the market opportunity

• Set clear goals, territories and partner portfolios for each team member, and hold the team accountable to pipeline, revenue and attach-rate outcomes

• Establish the team's operating cadence: one-on-ones, weekly pipeline reviews, deal inspection, partner QBRs and quarterly business planning

• Coach the team on executive engagement, joint business planning and co-selling in Japanese enterprise accounts, and model those behaviours personally

Set and own the Japan partner strategy

• Define which partner segments, partners and motions Anthropic prioritises in Japan, and in what sequence, based on revenue potential, customer reach and strategic fit

• Design the partner coverage model across our partner landscape (NTT DATA, Fujitsu, NEC, Hitachi, Accenture and others), and where we go deep vs. broad.

• Localise Anthropic's global partner program for Japan, including tiers, incentives, enablement paths and rules of engagement, and feed Japan requirements back into the global program design

• Own the annual and quarterly partner business plan for Japan and report on it to International Partnerships leadership

Lead our most strategic partnerships

• Own the executive relationships with Anthropic's most consequential partners in Japan, from joint business planning through to board-level sponsorship on both sides

• Negotiate and structure partnership agreements, including resale, co-development and revenue-sharing constructs, working with Legal, Finance and Deal Desk

• Lead the creation of joint solutions and industry offerings with partner practices in manufacturing, financial services, retail, telecommunications, life sciences and the public sector

Own partner pipeline, revenue and attach rate

• Carry the Japan partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and revenue targets, and the partner attach-rate target, for the team

• Run a disciplined forecast with the team and with Japan sales leadership, ensuring partner deals are registered, progressed and closed with predictability

• Decide where to deploy partner investments (market development funds, enablement, co-marketing, headcount) for the highest return

• Build the reporting and systems hygiene that gives International Partnerships and Anthropic leadership a clear, trusted view of the Japan partner business

Represent Japan and drive cross-functional execution

• Act as the single point of accountability for the partner business in Japan with Japan sales leadership, the Applied AI organisation, Marketing, Legal and Product

• Ensure Japanese partner and customer requirements, including language, data residency, security and sovereignty needs, are understood and prioritised by global product and engineering teams

• Partner with the Japan sales leader to embed partners into account planning and co-selling for the country's priority accounts

• Resolve channel conflict between direct sales, SIs and resellers, and set the rules of engagement that keep the ecosystem healthy as it grows

Be the face of Anthropic's partner ecosystem in Japan

• Represent Anthropic at partner executive forums, industry conferences and analyst engagements related to the partner ecosystem

• Sponsor the development of Japanese customer success stories, delivered with partners, that resonate with Japanese enterprise buyers

• Build Anthropic's reputation as the partner-first AI company in Japan through the way your team shows up every day

Minimum qualifications

• Experience in enterprise technology, with a substantial portion leading partner, alliances or channel businesses in Japan

• People leadership experience over partner or alliance teams, with a track record of hiring, developing and retaining strong performers

• Direct experience building a partner business in Japan for a US or global technology company, ideally through a period of rapid growth or market entry (hyperscaler, enterprise SaaS, data or AI platform)

• Proven ownership of partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue targets at a country or regional level, with the forecasting discipline to match

• Established executive relationships with Japan's major system integrators, consulting firms, and a reputation they would vouch for

• Experience negotiating complex partnership structures: resale agreements, joint solution development, and revenue-sharing or incentive models

• Demonstrated ability to operate as a player-coach, personally owning strategic relationships while building a team that scales beyond you

• Comfort shaping strategy in ambiguity and turning it into an operating plan, while working closely with global teams in other time zones

• Business-level fluency in Japanese and English, and the cultural fluency to move between Japanese enterprise norms and a fast-moving US company

• Based in Tokyo

Preferred qualifications

• 15 to 20+ years in enterprise technology leading partner, alliances or channel businesses in Japan and 5+ years of people leadership over partner or alliance teams
Experience with AI, data or cloud platform partnerships specifically, including partner-built solutions and marketplace motions

• Experience on the partner side, inside a Japanese SI or distributor, and an understanding of how those organisations make decisions

• Experience localising a global partner program for Japan and influencing its design

• Experience working alongside professional services or applied AI teams to deliver partner-led customer outcomes

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.
